doctrine: Central heat-pump water heaters (air-to-water, often paired with storage tanks) are the boring-proven electrification-ready DHW upgrade for multifamily central plants — spec them at boiler/water-heater end-of-life, not mid-life
Recirculation-loop controls (temperature setback, demand-based recirc pumping) are the low-cost, low-disruption first move before any equipment swap
Load-reduction first: low-flow fixtures and recirc-loop insulation reduce the DHW load the new plant has to be sized for

Measured baseline matters even for DHW: use metered gas/electric consumption tied to the water-heating end-use where sub-metered, or degree-day-normalized winter-summer delta as a proxy, before crediting modeled savings
Stage DHW plant replacement around boiler/tank end-of-life and capital events; a mid-life swap rarely clears the NOI test unless the existing plant is failing

Maintainability: central heat-pump water heaters need a maintenance contract the on-site or third-party engineer actually understands — confirm local service capacity before spec'ing an unfamiliar brand
origination_prompts: Does the PCA show the central water heater(s) or boiler(s) serving DHW nearing end-of-life or already flagged for replacement?
Is there a recirculation loop with no controls (constant-run pump, no setback)? Controls-first candidate.
Are fixtures original-to-construction (pre-2000) with no low-flow retrofit on record?
Does the property have electrical service headroom or a planned panel upgrade that would support a heat-pump water heater conversion?
feasibility_checks: Verify space and clearance for heat-pump water heater equipment (they need more footprint and ventilation air than a gas boiler of similar output)
Confirm electrical capacity for the heat-pump water heater's compressor load, especially in an all-gas building considering electrification
Check cold-climate performance derating for air-source heat-pump water heaters if the plant is not in conditioned space
Tenant disruption: recirc controls and equipment-room swaps are typically none/light; verify no unit-by-unit hot water outage is required during changeover
Check Shovels for local mechanical/plumbing contractors' experience with heat-pump water heater installs as a market-readiness signal
data_requirements: DHW plant inventory (type, capacity, install year, condition)
gas/electric billing history segmented or estimated for water heating
recirculation loop configuration and control status
